subject: Information Theory
title: Gene Regulatory Networks
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Gene Regulatory Networks.

hook.text: A human cell has about 20,000 genes, but only a fraction are active at any time. Regulatory networks decide which.

buildup.text: Genes regulate other genes through activators and repressors, forming complex Boolean-like logic circuits.

discovery.text: These networks process environmental signals and compute appropriate responses—gene expression as computation.

twist.text: The network topology constrains information flow. Feed-forward loops filter noise; feedback loops create memory.

climax.text: Cells are information processors. Their gene networks compute survival strategies from environmental data.

punchline.text: Genes regulate genes. Cells compute with chemistry.

quiz.question: What role do gene regulatory networks play?
options: They process signals and decide which genes to activate
